title: Base change and fppf target locality for smooth and surjective space maps
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Smoothness is tested on etale scheme charts using [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Surjectivity means surjectivity on the field-valued point classes of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Both smoothness and surjectivity, separately, are stable under arbitrary algebraic-space base change. Let $Y$ be a scheme and $\{Y_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ an fppf covering [def-pc-fppf-site]. Then $f$ is smooth if and only if every $X\times_YY_i\to Y_i$ is smooth, and $f$ is surjective if and only if every $X\times_YY_i\to Y_i$ is surjective. All fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. No quasi-compactness, finite type, or separation assumption on $f$ is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0429 (lemma-descending-property-smooth) and 041Q (lemma-descending-property-surjective), fppf specialization of fpqc locality; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 03ZE (lemma-base-change-smooth) and 03MH (lemma-base-change-surjective).

proof.text: Suppose $f$ is smooth and let $g:Y'\to Y$ be arbitrary. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to Y$ and a surjective etale scheme atlas $U\to E=X\times_YV$. The fibre-product and representable-etale calculus show that $U\to X$ is surjective etale. Thus $h:U\to V$ is smooth by the presentation criterion, whose scheme-property hypothesis is supplied by the scheme etale-locality lemma. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $V'\to Y'\times_YV$ and put $U'=U\times_VV'$. These are scheme fibre products, and $U'\to V'$ is smooth by scheme smooth base change. Indeed $U'\cong (U\times_YY')\times_{V\times_YY'}V'$: on a test scheme both sides consist of compatible triples $(u,y',v')$ with $v'$ mapping to $(h(u),y')$. Consequently $U'\to U\times_YY'$ and $U\times_YY'\to X\times_YY'$ are surjective etale by base change; their composite is a surjective etale scheme chart. Also $V'\to Y'$ is surjective etale. Apply the presentation criterion to the smooth scheme map $U'\to V'$ to conclude that $X\times_YY'\to Y'$ is smooth.

source.place: Tag 03ZE (lemma-base-change-smooth); remark-base-change-P and Tag 03MJ (lemma-local-source-target), expanded on scheme charts

proof.text: Suppose $f$ is surjective. For any field-valued representative $y':\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y'$, surjectivity in the extension-lifting formulation gives a field extension $K\hookrightarrow L$ and $x:\operatorname{Spec}L\to X$ with $f(x)=g(y')|_L$. The pair $(x,y'|_L)$ is a section of the sheaf fibre product $X\times_YY'$ over $L$ and maps to $y'|_L$. This proves surjectivity of the base change. Notice that an extension of $K$ is allowed; a lift over $K$ itself is not asserted.

source.place: Tag 03MH (lemma-base-change-surjective), using the common-field-extension proof of spaces-properties.tex Tag 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian)

proof.text: We will apply the scheme fpqc-family descent theorem with $P=$ smooth. Its base-change hypothesis is clause (2) of the scheme base-change lemma, and its descent hypothesis for one flat quasi-compact surjection is the scheme smooth fpqc-descent lemma. For its Zariski target-locality hypothesis, let $q:A\to B$ be a scheme morphism and let $(W_a)$ cover $B$ by opens and suppose $A\times_BW_a\to W_a$ is smooth for every $a$. For each $x\in A$ choose $a$ with $q(x)\in W_a$; the open inclusions $A\times_BW_a\to A$ and $W_a\to B$ are etale, so the pointwise condition (iii) of scheme etale source-and-target locality gives smoothness of $A\to B$. Conversely restrictions are smooth by base change. Hence all three hypotheses of the existing fpqc-family theorem hold, and smoothness of a scheme map descends from its pullbacks along any fpqc covering family. No quasi-compactness of that scheme map or of individual arrows of the family is required.

source.place: Tag 0429 (lemma-descending-property-smooth), reduction to scheme descent in descent.tex Tag 02VL (lemma-descending-property-smooth); the family assembly is the existing fpqc-family descent theorem

proof.text: Now assume $Y$ is a scheme, $(Y_i\to Y)$ is an fppf covering, and every $X_i=X\times_YY_i\to Y_i$ is smooth. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $a:U\to X$. Each $U_i=U\times_YY_i$ is a scheme, and $U_i\to X_i$ is surjective etale by the representable-etale calculus. With target chart $Y_i\to Y_i$ the presentation criterion therefore gives smoothness of the scheme map $U_i\to Y_i$. The given fppf family is an fpqc family by the fppf-to-fpqc covering lemma. Step 3 applied to $U\to Y$ proves it smooth; the presentation diagram $U\to Y$, $U\to X$, $Y\to Y$ then proves $f$ smooth. The converse is step 1.

source.place: Tag 0429 (lemma-descending-property-smooth), choose a scheme atlas and descend its composite to the scheme target; topologies.tex Tag 022C (lemma-zariski-etale-smooth-syntomic-fppf-fpqc)

proof.text: Assume instead that every $X_i\to Y_i$ is surjective. Given $y:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$, pull the fppf covering back to $\operatorname{Spec}K$. The covering-base-change lemma makes $(Y_i\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}K)$ jointly surjective on scheme points. Choose an index $i$ and a point $t$ above the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$. Its residue-field representative gives a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}L\to Y_i\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}K$, with $L=\kappa(t)$ a field extension of $K$. Surjectivity of $X_i\to Y_i$ then gives, after a further extension $L\hookrightarrow M$, a lift to $X_i$. Projecting this lift to $X$ gives $x$ with $f(x)=y|_M$, proving surjectivity of $f$. Conversely use step 2. If the index set is empty, the covering condition forces $Y$ empty, so there are no $y$ to test; smoothness in step 4 is likewise vacuous by the pointwise scheme criterion and the empty source atlas. Empty members of a nonempty covering cause no change.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_surjective_fppf_locality {S : Scheme.{u}} : (∀ {X Y Y' : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y), MapIsLocally (@Smooth) f → MapIsLocally (@Smooth) (enlargedFibreProductFst g f)) ∧ (∀ {X Y Y' : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y), IsJointlySurjective (fun _ : Unit ↦ f.hom.hom) → IsJointlySurjective (fun _ : Unit ↦ (enlargedFibreProductFst g f).hom.hom)) ∧ (∀ {I : Type w} (T : Over S) (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace T) (Tᵢ : I → Over S) (g : ∀ i : I, Tᵢ i ⟶ T), Presieve.ofArrows (fun i : I ↦ (Tᵢ i).left) (fun i : I ↦ (g i).left) ∈ Scheme.fppfPrecoverage T.left → (MapIsLocally (@Smooth) f ↔ ∀ i : I, MapIsLocally (@Smooth) (enlargedFibreProductFst (ObjectProperty.homMk ⟨yoneda.map (g i)⟩ : schemeSpace (Tᵢ i) ⟶ schemeSpace T) f))) ∧ (∀ {I : Type w} (T : Over S) (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace T) (Tᵢ : I → Over S) (g : ∀ i : I, Tᵢ i ⟶ T), Presieve.ofArrows (fun i : I ↦ (Tᵢ i).left) (fun i : I ↦ (g i).left) ∈ Scheme.fppfPrecoverage T.left → (IsJointlySurjective (fun _ : Unit ↦ f.hom.hom) ↔ ∀ i : I, IsJointlySurjective (fun _ : Unit ↦ (enlargedFibreProductFst (ObjectProperty.homMk ⟨yoneda.map (g i)⟩ : schemeSpace (Tᵢ i) ⟶ schemeSpace T) f).hom.hom)))
